column3: With respect to the Troy Towne Center Mortgage Loan (1.3%), the related Phase I ESA identifies as a controlled REC for the Mortgaged Property, the historic onsite presence of dry cleaning operations, which resulted in environmental impacts to the site. These impacts were identified during investigations that took place at the Mortgaged Property from 2009 to 2018. The Mortgaged Property was entered into the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency’s (“OEPA”) Voluntary Action Program (“VAP”) to address the identified impacts. Remedial actions taken at the Mortgaged Property include the excavation of impacted soils, conducting three vapor extraction events, and the installation, in December 2011, of a sub-slab depressurization system (“SSDS”) beneath the tenant space area historically occupied by the dry cleaning operations and a neighboring tenant space. The SSDS operated until 2014. On July 29, 2021, the OEPA issued a Covenant Not To Sue (“CNS”) to the Mortgaged Property, which provides regulatory closure under the VAP. The CNS includes an Environmental Covenant (“EC”) that requires the maintenance of a portion of the existing building slab foundation and a portion of the existing paved parking lot as engineering controls to address any residual environmental impacts remaining at the Mortgaged Property. The EC also restricts the Mortgaged Property to non-residential use and prohibits the extraction or use of groundwater. The Mortgaged Property has implemented an Operations & Maintenance Plan to ensure compliance with the engineering controls required by the EC. The Mortgaged Property also submits an annual compliance report to the OEPA to confirm compliance with the CNS and EC. The most recent annual compliance letter, dated August 18, 2025, documents that the Mortgaged Property is in compliance with the property restrictions and requirements imposed by the EC. Given that the Mortgaged Property has received regulatory closure under the VAP, and that any residual impacts are managed through engineering controls and use restrictions, the Phase I ESA consultant concluded that no further action was necessary in relation to this matter. However, the consultant recommends continued compliance with the on-going requirements of the EC that has been placed on the Mortgaged Property.
